located_point.method: Sentinel-2 composite renders at 4 km, 2 km, 1.2 km and 800 m (RGB, NIR, SWIR, brightness, edge). The site is the brick-red and bare-soil area of about 1.2 km by 1.2 km enclosed by modern tracks and embankments south of the Moenjodaro runway. Two light, cleared patches inside it (centres near 27.32718 N 68.13594 E and 27.32240 N 68.13608 E) lie 530 m apart almost due north-south, matching the separation and bearing of the DK-G and HR excavations on Mackay 1938 Plate I (600 m, nearly due south); the western brick-red patch near 27.32563 N 68.13292 E then falls where Plate I puts the Stupa mound. The located point is the middle of the lower town between these areas.

imagery_unmeasurable_reason: Features not resolvable at 10 m: no straight edge inside the mound could be tied to a wall, street or drain on the plans. The only straight boundaries are the edges of the cleared excavation patches, modern tracks and embankments, which are not lines under the rules.

notes: Imagery: located but not measurable at 10 m (see imagery_unmeasurable_reason). Plans: all three north arrows are unspecified, so every plan bearing is relative to its arrow and the true reference is unresolved. Marshall Pl. XXXIX (HR) shows street frontages in three orientation groups: most street faces of First Street, Street 2, Street 3 (north part), the drain lane and South Lane lie at +3.5 to +7.1 degrees from the plate's arrow (hr-main); High Lane, Deadman Lane and the southern part of Street 3 lie between -1.3 and +2.6 degrees (hr-near-zero); Lane 4 runs at about +10 degrees (hr-lane4). The frontage of Street 3 visibly bends near House XLV. The plate is a folding plan photographed flat; a crease runs north-south through Section B near x 750-790 px and no measured line crosses it. Mackay Pl. XIII panel C (DK-G, Late Period Ib and II): First Street and West Street frontages at +3.4 to +6.4 degrees, one Central Street face at +2.6 and the opposite face at -0.8 degrees; the arrow is short (78 px measured) and its error is carried into every line. Kenoyer Fig. 4.3: only the drawn line of DK-G First Street was identifiable as architecture at the figure's scale; the twin lines through HR are too irregular at 1.2 m per pixel and were not measured. The main plan systems of Marshall Pl. XXXIX (hr-main, +5.68) and Mackay Pl. XIII (dkg-main, +4.23) and the Kenoyer line (+4.65) agree within 1.5 degrees relative to their own arrows. The HR and DK-G plans show different parts of the town, so this agreement compares two quarters drawn under two different arrows. Jansen and Urban 1987 (Interim Reports 2) Figs. 6-8 on PDF pages 25 and 32 and Fig. 2 on PDF page 88 were inspected but not measured: Fig. 7 has a scale bar without legible values and Fig. 2 has no scale bar; Fig. 8 carries a drawn reconstruction grid, which is an interpretation and was not measured. Mackay 1938 Plate I (site plan) was used for identification only; its street lines are too coarse at the scan's resolution.
